name: start_recording
title: Start Recording
description: Start a background screen recording. Returns a session id; finalize it with stop_recording. Never auto-starts.

target.description: full | monitor:<index> (0 = primary) | window:<title> (or window:exe=<app.exe> / window:hwnd=<handle>) | region:<x>,<y>,<w>,<h>. window: captures the rectangle the window occupies as displayed (case-insensitive exact title, else substring; topmost match)

exactTitle.description: For window: targets, match only a window whose title equals the given title (case-insensitive); never fall back to a substring (default false)

audio.description: Audio capture (default none, video-only). source system needs a loopback device; microphone capture is not supported.

source.description: system captures what is playing on the machine; none is video-only

device.description: Optional dshow loopback device name (from list_audio_devices); auto-detected when omitted

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

maxDurationSec.description: Stop automatically after this many seconds, finalizing the file (default 3600, or SCREENCAST_MAX_RECORDING_SEC; at most 604800, 7 days). 0 = no cap

backend.description: gdigrab (default) records the screen rectangle. wgc (window: targets, FFmpeg 8+) records the window's own surface through Windows Graphics Capture: covered, moved, or background windows keep recording; frames only its client area. No audio with wgc

events.description: Also log mouse clicks, scroll, cursor positions, and typing to <recording>.events.jsonl, timed to the video and in video pixels (default false). Read it with read_events

keys.description: With events: masked (default) logs typing only as bursts (start and length on a 0.5 s grid), never which keys or per-key times; shortcuts also names Ctrl/Alt/Win chords (e.g. Ctrl+S) with their times. Typed text is never logged

replayBufferSec.description: Instant replay: keep only the last N seconds in a rolling ring of 2 s segments under SCREENCAST_HOME/replay (disk bounded to about N s); save_replay writes the last seconds to an mp4 without stopping it, and stop_recording discards the buffer unless save: true. gdigrab only

name: stop_recording
title: Stop Recording
description: Stop a recording gracefully so the file is finalized; returns the path and duration.

save.description: Replay-buffer sessions: write the whole buffer to outputPath before discarding it (default false: the buffer is discarded)

name: save_replay
title: Save Replay
description: Save the last N seconds of a replay buffer (start_recording replayBufferSec) to an mp4; the buffer keeps running.

sessionId.description: Session id of a recording started with replayBufferSec

lastSec.description: Seconds to keep, back from now (default: the whole buffer; capped at replayBufferSec)

output.description: Output .mp4 path (default under SCREENCAST_HOME/recordings). With an events buffer, the sliced <output>.events.jsonl is written beside it

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

reencode.description: Frame-exact re-encode (slower). Default: a near-instant stream copy that keeps up to one segment (2 s) of earlier frames hidden behind an edit list; never rely on it to remove secrets

name: list_sessions
title: List Sessions
description: List all recording sessions (active and finished) with their status, target, output path, and whether the process is still alive.

name: get_session
title: Get Session
description: Inspect a single recording session by id, including live status and whether its output file exists on disk.

name: read_events
title: Read Input Events
description: Read the input events (clicks, scroll, cursor, shortcuts, typing bursts) of a recording made with events: true, in video seconds and pixels; e.g. types: ['down'], then sample_frames there.

sessionId.description: Session id of a recording started with events: true

input.description: Or a recording path (its sibling .events.jsonl is read) or the .events.jsonl itself

from.description: Only events at or after this video time, in seconds

to.description: Only events at or before this video time, in seconds

types.description: Only these event types; clicks are down, key is a named shortcut, typing a burst of typing, gap a stretch where events may be missing

inFrameOnly.description: Drop events whose cursor was outside the recorded area

name: add_marker
title: Add Marker
description: Mark a labelled moment on a recording, live or at a second. Kept in the session and a sidecar; chapters and pipeline turn markers into chapters.

label.description: What happens here, e.g. "bug appears" or "step 3: save" (at most 200 characters)

sessionId.description: The recording to mark (running, or stopped with at)

input.description: Or a video path (needs at); the marker goes in its .markers.json sidecar

at.description: Video second to mark. Default: now, on the running recording's clock

name: review_recording
title: Review Recording
description: Open a recording for a person to review: in MCP Apps clients an inline player to scrub, trim, and redact, then export; elsewhere just the video's details.

sessionId.description: Or the session id of a stopped recording

name: player_frames
title: Player Frames
description: Preview frames for the review player: JPEGs on an even grid over the video plus frames at scene changes, with their real times. Used by the inline player; agents should use sample_frames or contact_sheet instead.

maxFrames.description: Frames on the even grid (default 120); scene-change frames come on top, up to as many again

name: screenshot
title: Take Screenshot
description: Capture one PNG of the screen, a monitor, a window, or a region, returned inline and by path.

target.description: full | monitor:<index> | window:<title> (or window:exe=<app.exe> / window:hwnd=<handle>) | region:<x>,<y>,<w>,<h>. window: captures the rectangle the window occupies as displayed (case-insensitive exact title, else substring; topmost match)

exactTitle.description: For window: targets, match only a window whose title equals the given title (case-insensitive); never fall back to a substring (default false)

backend.description: gdigrab (default) captures what is visible; wgc (window: targets, FFmpeg 8+) captures the window itself even when covered, via Windows Graphics Capture

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

returnImage.description: Also return the screenshot inline as a downscaled JPEG image (default true)

maxImageWidth.description: Downscale the inline image to at most this width (default 1280)

name: sample_frames
title: Sample Frames
description: Sample PNG frames from a video (by fps, timestamps, or scene changes) and return the first few inline so the model can see what happened.

input.description: Path to the source video file

mode.description: How to pick frames; scenes returns only frames where the screen changed (plus the first), strongest first up to maxFrames. Defaults to fps or timestamps, whichever is given

fps.description: Sample this many frames per second (mode fps)

timestamps.description: Explicit second offsets to grab one frame at each (mode timestamps)

sceneThreshold.description: Mode scenes: how much a frame must change to count, 0-1 (default 0.1)

dedupe.description: Mode fps: drop frames nearly identical to the previous one (default false)

outputDir.description: Optional folder for the frames (defaults under SCREENCAST_HOME/frames)

maxFrames.description: Most frames this call may write (default 100, max 1000); in fps mode a rate that would exceed it is lowered so frames still span the whole video

returnImages.description: Also return frames inline as downscaled JPEG images (default true)

maxInlineImages.description: How many frames to embed inline (default 8, max 20); every frame is still listed by path

maxImageWidth.description: Downscale inline images to at most this width (default 1280)

name: contact_sheet
title: Contact Sheet
description: Tile timestamped frames of a video into one image to see a whole recording at a glance (the cheapest first look).

count.description: How many frames to tile (default 12, max 48)

mode.description: even spreads frames across the video (default); scenes uses the opening frame plus the strongest scene changes

sceneThreshold.description: Mode scenes: how much a frame must change to count (default 0.1)

columns.description: Tiles per row (default: one row up to 4 tiles, then roughly square)

tileWidth.description: Width of each tile in px (default 320)

poster.description: Write one representative poster frame instead of a sheet

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

returnImage.description: Also return the sheet inline as a downscaled JPEG image (default true)

maxImageWidth.description: Downscale the inline image to at most this width (default 1280)

name: screen_diff
title: Screen Diff
description: Compare two screenshots or frames: SSIM score, changed share, and changed boxes in b's pixels, to check a UI change happened only where expected.

a.description: The before image (or video: its first frame)

b.description: The after image (or video); scaled to a's size if it differs

pixelThreshold.description: How different (0-255 mean) a cell of about 32x32 image pixels must be to count as changed (default 12)

returnImage.description: Also return b inline with changed regions outlined (default true)

name: wait_for_change
title: Wait for Screen Change
description: Wait until part of the screen changes or settles, instead of guessing a sleep. Returns the elapsed time, changed regions (screenshot pixels; add `origin` for desktop), and the final state.

target.description: full | monitor:<index> | window:<title> (or window:exe=<app.exe> / window:hwnd=<handle>) | region:<x>,<y>,<w>,<h>

exactTitle.description: For window: targets, match the title exactly (default false)

mode.description: change (default): return when the target differs from the start; settle: return once it has stopped changing for settleSec

timeoutSec.description: Give up after this many seconds (default 30, max 600); a timeout is a normal result

settleSec.description: Mode settle: how long the screen must stay still (default 1)

pixelThreshold.description: How different (0-255 mean) a cell of about 32x32 screen pixels must be to count as changed (default 12)

returnImage.description: Also return a screenshot of the final state inline (default true)

keep.description: Keep the final screenshot on disk and return its path (default false: only returned inline)

name: find_text
title: Find Text (OCR)
description: OCR (built into Windows) on the screen, an image, or video frames, with line and match boxes in image pixels (add `origin` for desktop coordinates). Locate UI text or secrets (e.g. regex 'sk-|ghp_|api.?key') to redact. Best-effort: review results.

target.description: Read live from the screen: full | monitor:<index> | window:<title> (or window:exe=<app.exe> / window:hwnd=<handle>) | region:<x>,<y>,<w>,<h> (one of target / input)

input.description: Or read from an image or video file

timestamp.description: For a video input: the second to read (default 0)

scanEverySec.description: For a video input: read a frame every N seconds across the whole clip; each match gets its time and redactRegions get start/end

maxFrames.description: With scanEverySec: most frames to read (default 30)

exactTitle.description: For window: targets, match the title exactly (default false)

backend.description: For a live target: gdigrab (default) reads what is visible; wgc (window: targets, FFmpeg 8+) reads the window itself even when covered

query.description: Text to look for; case-insensitive and tolerant of OCR misreads (_ vs -, I vs l, O vs 0; regexes get the _ vs - tolerance)

regex.description: Treat query as a regular expression

redact.description: Also return padded rectangles around matches, ready for redact_region

keep.description: For a live target: keep the captured screenshot and return its path (default false: deleted after reading)

returnImage.description: Return the image inline with matches outlined (default true when there is a query)

name: get_media_info
title: Get Media Info
description: Probe a media file with ffprobe and return duration, resolution, frame rate, codecs, container format, and size.

input.description: Path to the media file to probe

name: trim
title: Trim Video
description: Cut a video down to one sub-clip by start + (end or duration). For several segments use clip; to combine with other edits use pipeline.

end.description: End time in seconds (use end OR duration)

duration.description: Clip length in seconds (use end OR duration)

exact.description: Re-encode so nothing before start stays in the file (default true); false stream-copies and keeps hidden frames

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: concat
title: Concatenate Videos
description: Join videos end to end with hard cuts: stream copy when they match, else a re-encode (`mode` says which). For transitions use xfade_transition or assemble_highlights.

inputs.description: Two or more video paths to join, in order

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: convert
title: Convert Format
description: Convert media to mp4, webm, or gif. For a size-bounded GIF/WebP prefer export_gif; for a smaller mp4, compress or export_preset.

width.description: Output width in px, height auto (gif only; default 720)

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: export_gif
title: Export GIF or WebP
description: Export an animated GIF or WebP that fits a size budget (for PRs, issues, READMEs), stepping fps, width, and quality down until it fits.

format.description: gif (default) or webp (animated WebP, usually much smaller)

start.description: Start at this many seconds into the video

duration.description: Export only this many seconds (default: to the end)

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: crop
title: Crop Video
description: Crop a video to a pixel rectangle; one running off the frame is rejected.

x.description: Left edge of the crop in pixels

y.description: Top edge of the crop in pixels

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: scale
title: Scale Video
description: Resize a video to a target width and/or height and re-encode. Provide one side to keep the aspect ratio, or both to set an exact size.

width.description: Target width in px (omit to derive from height)

height.description: Target height in px (omit to derive from width)

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: speed
title: Change Speed
description: Change playback speed by a factor (>1 faster, <1 slower) and re-encode. Audio is retempo'd to match when the source has an audio track.

factor.description: Speed multiplier: >1 faster, <1 slower (2 = double speed)

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: overlay
title: Overlay Image or Video
description: Composite an image or video (logo, watermark, picture-in-picture) onto a video at a pixel position, optionally scaled and time-limited; keeps the base's audio and length.

overlay.description: Path to the overlay image or video

width.description: Optional overlay width in px (height auto)

height.description: Optional overlay height in px (width auto)

start.description: Optional second to show the overlay from

end.description: Optional second to hide the overlay after

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: callout
title: Add Callouts
description: Annotate a video with timed boxes, text labels, and arrows. Fallback fonts used are listed in fallbackFonts; characters no font covers are reported in warnings.

items.description: Annotations drawn in order (later on top). box: {type, x, y, width, height, thickness?, fill?}; text: {type, x, y, text, size?, background?}; arrow: {type, x1, y1, x2, y2 (head), thickness?}. All take from?, to? (seconds) and color?

fontFile.description: Font for the text: a .ttf/.otf/.ttc path, or a file name in C:\Windows\Fonts (e.g. msyh.ttc). Default: the bundled Inter, or a Windows system font that covers characters Inter lacks (CJK, emoji, Arabic, Hebrew, Indic, Thai, ...)

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: keystroke_overlay
title: Keystroke Overlay
description: Burn keycast-style badges for shortcuts, clicks, and typing from the recording's input event log (start_recording events: true). Never shows typed text: the log has none.

events.description: Event log (default: the input's .events.jsonl from start_recording events: true)

clicks.description: Show clicks, double clicks, and right clicks (default true)

typing.description: Show typing bursts as "Typing…" (default true); typed text is never logged

keys.description: shortcuts (default): the logged chord (Ctrl + S, repeats as ×N); masked: its modifiers only (Ctrl + …). Shortcuts are only logged with start_recording keys: "shortcuts"

lingerSec.description: Seconds a badge stays up after its input (default 1.2); the next badge replaces it

position.description: Where the badge sits (default bottom, centred)

size.description: Font size px (default 4.5% of the frame height)

color.description: Text color (default white), on the same dark panel as a callout

fontFile.description: Font for the badges: a .ttf/.otf/.ttc path or a C:\Windows\Fonts file name. Default: the bundled Inter, with a covering system font as fallback

dryRun.description: Return the planned badges; write nothing

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: backdrop
title: Add Backdrop
description: Frame a video or screenshot on a gradient, color, or wallpaper with padding, rounded corners, and a drop shadow, optionally on a 16:9/1:1/9:16/4:5 canvas.

input.description: Path to the source video, or an image (png/jpg) for a framed still

preset.description: Gradient look in the project's palette: desktop (default, dark slate), rec (record red), amber (amber to red), light (pale, for light UIs)

colors.description: Instead of a preset: 1 color = solid, 2-4 = a diagonal gradient (name or #RRGGBB)

image.description: A wallpaper image instead, scaled to cover the canvas

padding.description: Space around the content in px (default 6% of the longer side)

radius.description: Corner radius px (default about 1.2% of the longer side; 0 = square)

shadow.description: Drop shadow blur px (default about 2.5% of the longer side; 0 = none)

aspect.description: Put the result on this aspect's canvas (1920x1080, 1080x1920, 1080x1080, 1080x1350), content scaled to fit inside the padding

output.description: Optional output path (defaults under SCREENCAST_HOME/edits, or screenshots for an image)

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: compress
title: Compress Video
description: Re-encode a video smaller (H.264 CRF ladder, optional width cap). For a platform target use export_preset.

maxWidth.description: Optional width cap in px; only ever downscales

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: extract_audio
title: Extract Audio
description: Extract the audio track of a media file to its own file (mp3, aac, wav, or copy). Returns the output path.

format.description: Audio output codec; copy keeps the source codec without re-encoding

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: normalize_audio
title: Normalize Loudness
description: Normalize loudness to a delivery target (two-pass EBU R128 loudnorm); video is copied. Reports loudness before and after.

input.description: Path to the source video or audio file

target.description: youtube (-14 LUFS, default), podcast (-16), broadcast (EBU R128, -23), or a LUFS number such as -18

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: denoise
title: Denoise Audio
description: Reduce steady background noise (fan, hum, hiss) in a recording's audio with an adaptive FFT denoiser. Video is copied untouched. Returns the output path.

input.description: Path to the source video or audio file

strength.description: How hard to reduce noise: light (6 dB), medium (12 dB, default), strong (20 dB)

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: transcribe
title: Transcribe Speech
description: Transcribe a recording's speech to an SRT subtitle file, locally, with FFmpeg 8's whisper filter (needs a whisper.cpp model file). Returns the SRT path and the text. Pair with burn_subtitles to caption the video.

input.description: Path to the video or audio to transcribe

model.description: Path to a whisper.cpp model file (ggml-*.bin); defaults to SCREENCAST_WHISPER_MODEL

language.description: Spoken language code, e.g. en, or auto (default)

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: burn_subtitles
title: Burn In Subtitles
description: Burn SRT/ASS subtitles (e.g. from transcribe) into a video in the bundled font.

subtitles.description: Path to an .srt or .ass subtitle file

style.description: clean (default for .srt): a modest outlined line; social: large bold text on a dark box. An .ass/.ssa file keeps its own styling unless a style is given

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: chapters
title: Chapters
description: Write chapters (markers, scene changes, transcript, or a list) into an mp4/mkv/mov copy without re-encoding; returns YouTube chapter text. Can mux an SRT as soft subtitles.

sessionId.description: Or a stopped recording's session id (uses its markers)

from.description: Where chapters come from (ignored with chapters): markers (default; add_marker, else the file's own chapters), scenes (strongest screen changes), or transcript (an SRT, split at pauses)

chapters.description: Explicit chapters, { start (s), title }, instead of from

minChapterSec.description: Shortest chapter; closer points merge (default 1, or 10 for scenes and 30 for transcript). Scenes picks at most 12 chapters, the strongest screen changes

subtitles.description: Also mux this .srt/.vtt/.ass as a soft (toggleable) subtitle track (mov_text in mp4/mov), instead of burning it in

subtitleLanguage.description: ISO 639-2 language of subtitles, e.g. eng

textOnly.description: Only return the chapters and YouTube text; write no file

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: clip
title: Extract Clips
description: Extract several frame-exact segments, each to its own file. For one segment, trim does the same.

segments.description: One or more {start, end} segments; each becomes its own output file

output.description: Optional output path (single segment only; multi-segment lands under SCREENCAST_HOME/edits)

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: cut_idle
title: Cut Idle Stretches
description: Remove dead air: cut stretches where the screen is frozen (and silent), keeping a short pad. Returns the time saved.

minIdleSec.description: Only cut still stretches at least this long (default 2)

keepSec.description: Keep this much of each stretch at both edges (default 0.4)

useAudio.description: Idle only if the audio is also silent (default true when there is audio)

dryRun.description: Only report the stretches that would be cut

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: redact_region
title: Redact Regions
description: Cover given rectangles in a video (e.g. secrets on screen). Not automatic detection: find them with find_text redact: true. Off-frame regions are rejected.

start.description: Optional second to start redacting from

end.description: Optional second to stop redacting after

regions.description: One or more rectangles to redact; each may be limited to a time window

style.description: box (default) draws an irreversible solid fill; blur and pixelate are softer but partially recoverable

pad.description: Optional pixels to expand each region by, to cover anti-aliased edges (default 0)

color.description: Fill color for box style (default black)

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: list_audio_devices
title: List Audio Devices
description: List DirectShow audio devices and flag a likely loopback (Stereo Mix or a virtual-audio driver), for start_recording's audio.device.

name: list_targets
title: List Capture Targets
description: List the desktop, monitors, and visible windows (topmost first, with capturability per backend). Each entry has a `target` string to pass as-is to capture tools; use it instead of guessing a title.

exe.description: Only list windows of this executable, e.g. Code.exe or code

titleContains.description: Only list windows whose title contains this text (case-insensitive)

capturableOnly.description: Leave out windows neither backend can capture (minimized, off screen). Default false

name: doctor
title: Check Setup
description: Check the setup: ffmpeg/ffprobe (FFmpeg 8+?), optional filters, capture devices, Windows OCR, settings, and enabled toolsets; `problems` says what is missing and how to fix it. Call on first use or when a tool reports a missing feature.

name: xfade_transition
title: Crossfade Transition
description: Join two videos with an xfade transition (audio crossfaded); they need not match in size, fps, or audio. For more clips use assemble_highlights.

transition.description: xfade transition name (default fade): fade, wipeleft, slideup, circleopen, dissolve, ...

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: assemble_highlights
title: Assemble Highlights
description: Stitch clips (including title cards) into one video with cuts or xfade transitions; they need not match in size, fps, or audio.

clips.description: Two or more clip paths, in order

transition.description: 'cut' (default, hard cuts) or an xfade transition name (fade, wipeleft, slideup, ...)

duration.description: Transition length in seconds when not a cut (default 1)

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: title_card
title: Title Card
description: Generate a title card clip (centered text on a solid background, silent audio track) to stitch in with assemble_highlights. Uncoverable characters are reported in warnings.

fontFile.description: Font for the text: a .ttf/.otf/.ttc path, or a file name in C:\Windows\Fonts (e.g. msyh.ttc). Default: the bundled Inter, or a Windows system font that covers characters Inter lacks (CJK, emoji, Arabic, Hebrew, Indic, Thai, ...)

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: music_bed
title: Add Music Bed
description: Lay music under a video: looped or trimmed to length, faded, leveled, and mixed with any existing audio. Video is stream-copied.

music.description: Path to the music audio file (looped/trimmed to the video length)

musicVolume.description: Music level 0..1 (default 0.25 over existing audio, 0.8 alone)

duck.description: Duck the music under the original audio via a sidechain (default false)

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: reframe
title: Reframe Aspect Ratio
description: Re-aspect a video to 16:9, 9:16, 1:1, or 4:5 by padding or cropping.

fit.description: pad (default): scale to fit and letterbox. crop: scale to fill and center-crop.

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: zoom
title: Zoom and Pan
description: Smooth animated zoom-and-pan into the action and back out, from keyframes or planned from logged clicks or screen changes.

keyframes.description: Views to animate between: {t, x, y, width, height} fills the frame with that rectangle by time t; {t, full: true} zooms out. Omit to plan automatically (see follow)

maxZoom.description: Auto mode: the furthest it zooms in (default 2.5)

follow.description: Without keyframes: clicks zooms toward each click in the input event log (start_recording events: true), changes toward where the screen changed; auto (default) uses clicks when the log has any

events.description: Event log to read clicks from (default: the input's sibling .events.jsonl); must match the input's timeline and size

highlightClicks.description: Draw an expanding ring at each click from the event log (default false)

holdSec.description: Auto mode: stay zoomed this long after activity stops (default 2)

dryRun.description: Only return the planned keyframes; write nothing

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: pipeline
title: Edit Pipeline
description: Run several edits (trim, crop, scale, speed, redact, callout, keystroke_overlay, reframe, zoom, backdrop, then optionally export_preset or export_gif) in one ffmpeg pass: one re-encode, no intermediate files. Prefer it over chaining edit tools.

steps.description: Edits in order, each { op, ...the same options as its tool }: trim, crop, scale, speed, redact, callout, keystroke_overlay (badges re-timed through earlier trims and speed changes), reframe, zoom (keyframes), backdrop, and as the last step only export_preset or export_gif. Times and pixels in a step are on the timeline and frame as they are at that step

quality.description: Encoder preset for an mp4 result (default standard)

dryRun.description: Return the planned ffmpeg command and output size without running it

output.description: Optional output path. Defaults under SCREENCAST_HOME/edits

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

chapters.description: Write the input's markers (add_marker; else its own chapters) into the output as chapters, re-timed through trims and speed changes. Not for a GIF/WebP result

name: export_preset
title: Export for Platform
description: Encode a platform-ready H.264 file (aspect, fps, bitrate, faststart) for a named platform.

platform.description: Target platform (sets aspect, resolution, fps, bitrate). steam_trailer: 1080p H.264 High, padded 5.5 Mbps CBR, 48 kHz audio at -14 LUFS. vertical_reel: 1080x1920, footage centred over a blurred copy, audio at -14 LUFS

fit.description: How to fit the source into the platform aspect: pad (default) or crop

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: bug_report
title: Bug Report Package
description: Package a recording as a paste-ready repro folder: secret-scanned, redacted clip and GIF, contact sheet, steps from the event log, OCR'd errors, environment, report.md for gh issue create --body-file.

redact.description: Box out OCR-found secrets in every output (default true; needs Windows OCR)

secretPattern.description: Secret regex (default: API keys, tokens, password: values)

regions.description: Extra boxes (video px; start/end on the clip clock)

outputDir.description: Package folder (default: a new one in SCREENCAST_HOME/edits)

overwrite.description: Replace a report already in outputDir
